items.title: [PaddlingLight.com] 1865 St. Francis Canoe Launched
items.content_html:
Back in September, I wrote that I hadn’t seen any replicas built of the 1865 St. Francis 2-Fathom Canoe, which appears as Figure 80 in The Bark Canoes and Skin Boats of North America, until Evan B. sent me photos of his 1865 St. Francis Canoe build. Now, we have another cedar-strip replica built and on the water. Ph. Payen sent a few photos of his new canoe. He wrote: Please find herewith a couple of pictures of a 1865 St Francis canoe made out of white pine, a tad heavy (62 pounds). I left the plywood apron inside stem and stern, and covered them with fiberglass to make watertight compartments. Gunwales had to be steamed, but the result is worth it. I used it solo to this day, and I am not certain my wife will join me one day. We are absolute beginners in paddling, and I must admit that the first trials were quite wet. There does not seem to be any kind of secondary stability, but it moves effortlessly, and it is a very pleasant way to be on the water. When I made my 3D model based on the drawings in The Bark Canoes and Skin Boats of North America, I I couldn’t find any photos before I released the free canoe plans. Now we have two builders within months showing off their builds. That’s amazing. Thanks to Ph. Payen for sending these over. The canoe looks amazing!

The post 1865 St. Francis Canoe Launched appeared first on PaddlingLight.com. You can leave a comment by clicking here: 1865 St. Francis Canoe Launched.

items.title: [guillaumemeigniez.me] Japanese Postcards
items.content_html: Along my trip across Japan I collected a bunch of postcards from places I visited. I got them in museums, in tourist shops or in second-hand bookstores. I sent some to friends and family, but most of them I kept as souvenirs for this year of travelling. I built a small website to showcase them in an interactive way organized by category. Very cool cities Osaka, Nagasaki, Kobe, Sapporo, Aomori, Fukushima... Favorite activity this year: hiking Mount Rokko (六甲山) & Mount Hiei (比叡山) in the Kyoto region, Mount Ni
